blocks.name: Content Overview and Layout
blocks.description: Patterns for structuring and presenting complex or high-volume content

blocks.name: Feedback
blocks.description: Patterns that inform users about system status, results, or errors

blocks.name: Forms and Input
blocks.description: Patterns that support efficient and accurate data entry through structured input mechanisms

blocks.name: Navigation
blocks.description: Patterns that guide users across or within the interface

blocks.name: Personalization
blocks.description: Patterns that let users customize content, layout, or features

blocks.name: Search and Filtering
blocks.description: Patterns that allow users to find and refine information by applying search queries or filters

blocks.name: Social Interaction
blocks.description: Patterns for communication, sharing, and collaboration among users

blocks.name: Visibility of System Status
blocks.description: The system should keep users informed about what is happening through appropriate and timely feedback

blocks.name: Match Between System and the Real World
blocks.description: The system should use language, concepts, and conventions familiar to users, reflecting real-world logic rather than system-oriented terms. This helps make interactions more intuitive

blocks.name: User Control and Freedom
blocks.description: Users should be able to easily exit or undo unintended actions, avoiding situations where they feel trapped

blocks.name: Consistency and Standards
blocks.description: Interfaces should follow platform and industry conventions, using consistent terms, actions, and layouts so that users do not have to guess what different elements mean

blocks.name: Error Prevention
blocks.description: The system should be designed to prevent errors from occurring in the first place by providing clear instructions, constraints, and validation before actions are taken

blocks.name: Recognition Rather Than Recall
blocks.description: Interfaces should minimize users’ memory load by making options, actions, and information visible or easily retrievable, instead of requiring them to remember details

blocks.name: Flexibility and Efficiency of Use
blocks.description: The interface should cater to both inexperienced and experienced users, allowing shortcuts or personalization to increase efficiency for frequent tasks

blocks.name: Aesthetic and Minimalist Design
blocks.description: Interfaces should avoid unnecessary information and visual clutter. Every added element should have a clear purpose and contribute to the user’s goals

blocks.name: Help Users Recognize, Diagnose, and Recover from Errors
blocks.description: Error messages should be clear, indicate the problem, and suggest constructive solutions, enabling users to recover without frustration

blocks.name: Help and Documentation
blocks.description: While the system should ideally be usable without documentation, it should provide accessible, concise, and task-focused help resources when needed
